newsitem.title: USA: NHL-POPULAR CENTER SAVARD RETIRES AS BLACKHAWKS PLAYER.
newsitem.headline: NHL-POPULAR CENTER SAVARD RETIRES AS BLACKHAWKS PLAYER.

text.p: Centre Denis Savard, one of the most popular players in the history of the Chicago Blackhawks, announced his retirement on Thursday.
Savard had 473 goals and 865 assists for 1,338 points in 1,196 career games over his 17-year NHL career.

The 36-year-old Savard, 17th on the NHL's all-time points list, had 377 goals and 719 assists for 1,096 points in 881 games with the Blackhawks, with whom he remains as both a developmental coach and in a community relations capacity.
Savard struggled through the 1996-97 season. He had just nine goals and 18 assists in 64 games with a minus-10 rating and had just two assists in six playoff games.
The third overall pick in the 1980 draft, Savard played the first 10 years of his career with Chicago and led the team in scoring seven consecutive seasons from 1981-82 to 1987-88.

The Blackhawks sent Savard to the Montreal Canadiens in exchange for defenceman Chris Chelios in June 1990. He played three seasons with Montreal and was a member of the Canadiens' 1993 Stanley Cup championship team.
The Tampa Bay Lightning signed Savard as a free agent in July 1993 and he played in 105 games for the Lightning over two seasons before being reacquired by Chicago in April 1995.
